competences: The learner identifies the four types of transport from pictures.
The learner relates transport to carrying people and goods.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, reads, spells and writes: transport, people, goods, road, water, railway, air.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to explain transport as moving people and goods.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to name the four types of transport.
priorKnowledge: The introduction checks learners’ familiarity with transport pictures and travel before introducing the names of the four types.
materials: Wall chart showing road, water, railway and air transport
Transport word cards: road, water, railway, air
references: P I Literacy Lesson Notes Term III
P I Literacy Scheme OF Work Term III

steps.content: Transport pictures and the starter question: What is transport?
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher displays wall chart showing road, water, railway and air transport and asks: "What is transport?" Learners first identify familiar pictures; the teacher connects their responses to meaning and types of transport.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners look at the transport pictures, identify familiar words, and give oral responses to the starter question before copying any notes.

steps.content: Meaning of transport: Transport is the movement of people and goods from one place to another.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher points to the relevant transport pictures and writes these points on the board: Transport is the movement of people and goods from one place to another. Using guided discussion, the teacher asks: "What is transport?" and checks that learners identify the corresponding pictures or words.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the pictures and words for meaning of transport, answer the quoted question, and copy the short points into their books.

source.quote: movement of people with their goods from one place to another

steps.content: Types of transport: Road transport Water transport Railway transport Air transport
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher points to the relevant transport pictures and writes these points on the board: Road transport Water transport Railway transport Air transport Using guided discussion, the teacher asks: "Name the four types of transport." and checks that learners identify the corresponding pictures or words.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the pictures and words for types of transport, answer the quoted question, and copy the short points into their books.

source.quote: There are four types of transport

steps.content: Uses of transport: Carrying people Carrying goods Carrying animals Carrying water
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher points to the relevant transport pictures and writes these points on the board: Carrying people Carrying goods Carrying animals Carrying water Using guided discussion, the teacher asks: "Give any two uses of transport." and checks that learners identify the corresponding pictures or words.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the pictures and words for uses of transport, answer the quoted question, and copy the short points into their books.

source.quote: Carrying people Carrying animal Carrying goods Carrying water

steps.content: 1. What is transport? 2. Name the four types of transport. 3. Give any two uses of transport.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher sets the sourced exercise: "What is transport?" "Name the four types of transport." "Give any two uses of transport." The teacher reads each item clearly, checks individual answers, and uses the transport chart to correct mistaken identifications.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the exercise questions in their books, complete any specified matching or drawing, and correct their responses with the teacher.

steps.content: Key points: Transport is the movement of people and goods from one place to another.; Road transport Water transport Railway transport Air transport; Carrying people Carrying goods Carrying animals Carrying water
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher checks the lesson objectives using these exercise items: "What is transport?" "Name the four types of transport." "Give any two uses of transport." The teacher confirms correct answers against the board notes and identifies learners needing further picture-supported practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners give short oral answers, compare them with the transport pictures and board notes, and correct any remaining errors in their books.

assessment: Check the written exercise and oral responses: What is transport? Name the four types of transport. Give any two uses of transport. Mark against the source-based answers and revisit incorrect identifications using the transport chart.
homework: Complete or correct this sourced exercise item in your book: Give any two uses of transport.
